title: A small Markdown converter
description:
Turn a little Markdown into HTML with regular expressions, line by line. This is how many real converters start. ```javascript markdownToHtml("# Notes\n\nSome **bold** and *soft* text with `code`.\n\n- one\n- [two](https://example.com)"); ``` ```html

Notes

Some bold and soft text with code.

  • one
  • two
``` Write two functions: **`inline(text)`** converts the inline parts of one line, in this order: 1. Escape `&`, `<` and `>` as `&`, `<` and `>`. 2. `` `code` `` becomes `code`; nothing inside code is converted further. 3. `**bold**` becomes `bold`. 4. `*soft*` becomes `soft`. 5. `[text](url)` becomes `text`. **`markdownToHtml(source)`** converts block by block and joins the output lines with `"\n"`: - `#` to `######` followed by a space make `

` to `

`; - consecutive lines starting with `- ` make one `
    ` with an `
  • ` per line; - consecutive other non-blank lines are joined with a space into one `

    `; - blank lines separate blocks; - inline conversion applies inside headings, list items and paragraphs.
hints: Write `inline` first and test it alone. The trick for code spans: `text.split(/(`[^`]*`)/)` keeps the code spans as separate pieces (the capturing group keeps the separators), so you can convert every piece except those.
Run the bold rule before the italic one: otherwise `*` would eat half of each `**`. The lazy `.+?` stops at the first closing marker.

For the blocks, keep two buffers, the current paragraph lines and the current list items, and a `flush()` that writes whichever is non-empty. Call it on a blank line, before a heading, and when switching between a list and a paragraph.
requirements: `inline` uses regular expressions with `replace`, and code spans are protected from the other rules.
Headings, lists and paragraphs are recognised and grouped as described.
HTML special characters in the input are always escaped.
stretch: Numbered lists (`1. item` into `<ol>`), fenced code blocks between ` ``` ` lines, and a Node.js script (lesson 7.06) that converts a `.md` file into an `.html` file.
